title: The Tithe
lead: A tenth of produce or income given to God. Abraham gave a tenth to Melchizedek and Jacob vowed one at Bethel; the law of Moses made tithes support the Levites, the poor and festival worship (Genesis 14:20; 28:22; Numbers 18:21; Deuteronomy 14:22–29).

sections.b: Before the law, Abraham tithes from war spoils (Genesis 14:20) and Jacob promises a tenth of all God gives him (28:22). The law gives the tithe to the Levites (Numbers 18:21–24), sets aside a tithe to be eaten in joy at the sanctuary (Deuteronomy 14:22–27) and a third-year tithe for the Levite, foreigner, orphan and widow (Deuteronomy 14:28–29). Malachi accuses Israel of robbing God in tithes (Malachi 3:8–10). Jesus criticizes tithing herbs while neglecting "justice, mercy and faithfulness" (Matthew 23:23), and Hebrews uses Abraham's tithe to argue Melchizedek's greatness (Hebrews 7:4–10). Christians differ on whether the tithe is binding today.
